customer_problem: Analysts swivel-chair between a chat assistant and a thick-client ERP or ticket system. Any automation today would mean a shared password and unlogged writes. The intake asks for a scoped four-week pilot that can read — and carefully write — a legacy system of record through a typed tool interface.

sow.title: Legacy system-of-record assistant — four-week pilot
sow.problem: Give an assistant a safe, allowlisted interface to a fictional legacy SOAP/RPC system so users can look up records and propose updates without a raw pipe to destructive methods.
users: Approver (commits to the system of record)
constraints: Fictional records only; no production ERP connectivity
Deny-by-default for methods not on the allowlist

goals: Stand up a mock SOAP service and a typed tool contract
Add a two-phase write path (propose, then commit)
Enforce the allowlist and wire an optional human approval on commit
Package a client config, audit viewer, and pilot readout

out_of_scope: A real SAP, Oracle, or other vendor connection
Replacing the legacy client for all users

pilot_plan.baseline: Lookups and updates happen in a thick client. Informal copy-paste into a chat tool is unlogged. There is no allowlist or dry-run for automated writes.
success_measures: 100% of non-allowlisted methods are denied in contract tests
Every write produces a dry-run diff and an audit record before commit
Commit cannot proceed without an explicit confirmation (and an approval id when enabled)
pilot_plan.first_shippable_slice: Read tools plus a two-phase write against a mock SOAP service, with deny-by-default and a published client config.

threat_model.summary: The pilot must not become an unauthenticated, unlogged back door into a system of record, even when that system is a mock.

items.threat: A caller invokes tools without a user or task identity.
items.mitigation: Require a user-bound credential on every tool call; reject anonymous traffic.

items.threat: A proposed update is altered between dry-run and commit.
items.mitigation: Bind commit to the dry-run hash and expire stale proposals.

items.threat: A record changes and no one can show which tool call did it.
items.mitigation: Append-only audit with tool name, actor, payload, and result.

items.threat: The model echoes fields a given user should not see.
items.mitigation: Filter tool results by role and keep raw SOAP out of logs by default.

items.threat: A looping agent floods the legacy mock or the real interface later.
items.mitigation: Rate limits, timeouts, and idempotency keys on writes.

items.threat: The agent calls a delete or admin method that was never granted.
items.mitigation: Deny-by-default allowlist and contract tests for disallowed methods.

architecture.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  User[Analyst] --> Agent[Assistant]
  Agent --> MCP[Typed tool server]
  MCP --> Policy[Allowlist and schema]
  Policy --> Adapter[Legacy SOAP adapter]
  Adapter --> Mock[Mock system of record]
  Policy --> Audit[Audit log]
  Policy -.-> Approver[Optional human approval]
architecture.caption: The assistant never talks to the legacy API directly. A typed tool layer applies allowlist, schema, dry-run, and audit policy first.

success_metrics.name: Allowlist enforcement
success_metrics.how_measured: Contract test suite against the mock service

success_metrics.name: Write safety
success_metrics.baseline: Unlogged direct edits in a thick client
success_metrics.target: Every write has a dry-run diff and an audit record
success_metrics.how_measured: Audit log review of the demo script

success_metrics.name: Time to look up a record
success_metrics.baseline: Swivel-chair between chat and thick client
success_metrics.target: Lookup completed in one assistant turn on fixture records
success_metrics.how_measured: Timed walkthrough on the sample data
